summary: Tested wire drag-to-position on /studio. Drag overlay mounts correctly when a design is loaded, hides when no design. All drag handles render per design.operation. Drag interactions (via dispatched PointerEvents) commit x/y into design.operations on pointer-up, exactly one /api/studio/render call fires per drag, x/y are clamped to [0..1] for overshoots in all four directions, both shape and text operations drag correctly, the Elements editor X/Y sliders still drive the overlay, hover ring is cyan, drag ring is orange, and the overlay realigns after window resize. NOTE: anonymous flow does NOT work because /api/studio/render requires auth (401 for anonymous), so no SVG → no bounds → overlay returns null. Testing performed with an injected community/buyer JWT.

integration_issues.issue: Reviewer instructions claim anonymous OK, but /api/studio/render is auth-gated (returns 401 for anonymous). With no SVG rendered, DragOverlay.bounds is null and the overlay returns null. So anonymous users cannot actually use drag. Needs either anonymous-friendly preview rendering or doc correction.

action_items: Optional: decide if /studio drag preview should work for anonymous users. Either (a) let /api/studio/render accept anonymous (with quota), or (b) update the agent-to-agent context note since anonymous truly cannot test drag visually.

Optional UX nit: page.mouse-driven drag tests (Playwright synthetic mouse) work fine when the handle is in viewport, but the preview canvas is laid out such that handles often sit below the fold after template load. A scrollIntoView on first template load would make the new drag feature instantly visible to users (and easier to test with synthesized mouse).
critical_code_review_comments: DragOverlay correctly debounces and fires only ONE /api/studio/render per pointer-up (verified via network interception).
Clamping in finishDrag works for all four edges (verified 4× via huge overshoot drags — final x/y land at exactly 0.0 or 1.0).
Slider → handle visual sync works (slider set to 0.9 moves the handle bbox right).
Handle class transitions correctly: hover applies ring-[#00ffff], during drag applies ring-[#ff4500] + bg-[#ff4500]/5.
Window resize re-measures bounds and keeps handle aligned within the SVG (verified post-resize handle center still inside SVG bounding box).
No drag layer renders when no design is loaded (verified true on a fresh /studio with cleared design).

Minor: only Playwright's `page.mouse.*` synthesized events do NOT reliably trigger the drag because the handle is often outside the viewport after template load (preview is below the fold). Native PointerEvent dispatch works perfectly. Not a code bug — the feature works for real users — but worth a scrollIntoView on first design load.
test_credentials: Injected community-buyer JWT for drag-test2@craftersmarket.org generated via /api/community/auth/magic/verify with accept_eua=true & eua_version=2026-04. Stored as localStorage.cm_buyer_jwt.
seed_data_creation: Created community user drag-test2@craftersmarket.org for testing.
context_for_next_testing_agent: /studio drag is auth-gated because the SVG preview comes from /api/studio/render which requires a community/maker JWT. To test, generate a magic token via backend/maker_auth.py issue_buyer_magic_token(email), POST to /api/community/auth/magic/verify with {token, accept_eua:true, eua_version:'2026-04'}, store the returned JWT as localStorage.cm_buyer_jwt, then reload /studio and click a template button (e.g., button[data-testid=studio-template-lake-house]). Drag handles only render once an SVG is in the preview container. Synthetic page.mouse drags often fail because the preview is below the fold after template load — use dispatchEvent with PointerEvent (pointerdown on the handle, pointermove + pointerup on the layer, with composed:true and pointerId/isPrimary set) for deterministic tests, OR scroll the drag layer into view first.
rca of the issue: No actual feature bug. The earlier-iteration tester's `page.mouse + element.bounding_box` mismatch was real: after a template load the design preview canvas sits below the viewport fold, so element.bounding_box returns negative/clipped client coords and Playwright's mouse can't hit the handle. Switching to direct PointerEvent dispatch (or scrollIntoView before drag) makes everything pass: state commits on pointer-up, render fires exactly once, clamping holds, text+shape ops both move, slider↔handle sync is bidirectional.
